title: 小明的新朋友
body:
今天是星期天，天气很好。小明去公园玩，看见一个男孩坐在地上。小明走过去说：“你好！我是小明。”男孩笑着说：“你好！我叫李华。”他们很快成了朋友。

李华有点渴，小明给他水喝。李华说：“谢谢！”然后他们一起去吃面条。吃完以后，他们在公园跑步，玩得很高兴。小明说：“明天见！”李华说：“明天见，朋友！”
translation: Today is Sunday and the weather is nice. Xiao Ming goes to the park to play and sees a boy sitting on the ground. Xiao Ming walks over and says, "Hello! I am Xiao Ming." The boy smiles and says, "Hello! My name is Li Hua." They quickly become friends.

Li Hua is a little thirsty, so Xiao Ming gives him water to drink. Li Hua says, "Thank you!" Then they go together to eat noodles. After eating, they run in the park and have a lot of fun. Xiao Ming says, "See you tomorrow!" Li Hua says, "See you tomorrow, friend!"

title: 新朋友
body:
今天是星期日，天气很好。小王去公园，看见一个男孩。小王说：“你好！我是小王。”男孩说：“你好！我是小李。”他们一起走路，看见一个商店。小王说：“我渴了，想买水。”小李说：“我也渴了。”他们买了两瓶水，一起喝。小王说：“谢谢你的水。”小李说：“不客气，我们是朋友了！”

后来，他们饿了，一起去吃饭。小李说：“我喜欢吃面，你吃什么？”小王说：“我也喜欢吃面。”他们吃了很多面，很高兴。小李说：“明天见，朋友！”小王说：“明天见！”
translation: Today is Sunday, and the weather is nice. Xiao Wang goes to the park and sees a boy. Xiao Wang says, "Hello! I am Xiao Wang." The boy says, "Hello! I am Xiao Li." They walk together and see a shop. Xiao Wang says, "I am thirsty and want to buy water." Xiao Li says, "I am thirsty too." They buy two bottles of water and drink together. Xiao Wang says, "Thank you for your water." Xiao Li says, "You're welcome, we are friends now!"

Later, they are hungry and go to eat together. Xiao Li says, "I like to eat noodles, what do you eat?" Xiao Wang says, "I also like to eat noodles." They eat a lot of noodles and are very happy. Xiao Li says, "See you tomorrow, friend!" Xiao Wang says, "See you tomorrow!"

title: 一次特别的讨论
body:
去年夏天，我的朋友小王邀请我去他的家乡。那是一个环境很好的小城市，空气新鲜，周围有很多山和河。小王在那里长大，对家乡非常有感情。他建议我一起去看看，说这是一个很好的机会了解中国不同的地方。

到了那里以后，我们参加了一个关于旅游的讨论会。会上有很多有经验的人分享他们的故事。小王也讲了他的经验，说他决定留在家乡工作，因为这里的环境让他感到很舒服。听了他的想法，我也开始思考自己的未来。

离开之前，小王给了我一些建议。他说每个人都要自己做决定，但是应该多听听别人的经验。这次旅行让我学到了很多，也让我明白环境对人的影响真的很大。我很感谢小王给了我这个机会，让我有了新的想法。
translation: Last summer, my friend Xiao Wang invited me to his hometown. It was a small city with a very good environment—fresh air, with many mountains and rivers all around. Xiao Wang grew up there and had deep feelings for his hometown. He suggested that I go with him to see it, saying this was a great opportunity to learn about different parts of China.

After arriving there, we attended a discussion meeting about tourism. Many experienced people shared their stories at the meeting. Xiao Wang also talked about his experience, saying he had decided to stay and work in his hometown because the environment there made him feel very comfortable. Hearing his thoughts, I also began to think about my own future.

Before leaving, Xiao Wang gave me some suggestions. He said everyone has to make their own decisions, but should listen to other people's experiences more. This trip taught me a lot and also made me understand that environment really has a big influence on people. I am very grateful to Xiao Wang for giving me this opportunity and giving me new ideas.

因为他的父母要求他留下来

title: 我的第一次工作机会
body:
去年夏天，我得到了一个很好的机会，可以去一家环保公司工作。这家公司的工作环境非常好，同事们都很友好。第一天上班的时候，经理对我说：“虽然你没有很多经验，但是我们愿意教你。”我听了以后觉得很高兴，也有一点紧张。

上班的第一个星期，我和同事们一起讨论了很多问题。有一次，我们讨论怎么保护城市的环境。一位有经验的同事给了我一些建议，他说我应该多学习，多观察。我把他的建议记在了本子上。每天下班后，我都会想一想今天学到了什么。

三个月后，我做出了一个重要的决定：我要继续在这家公司工作。因为这里的环境让我很舒服，而且我有机会学到很多东西。这段经验对我来说非常宝贵。现在，我也能给新来的同事提建议了。我觉得帮助别人是一件很快乐的事情。
translation: Last summer, I got a great opportunity to work at an environmental protection company. The working environment at this company was very good, and my colleagues were all very friendly. On my first day, the manager told me, 'Although you don't have much experience, we are willing to teach you.' After hearing this, I felt very happy but also a little nervous.

During my first week at work, I discussed many issues with my colleagues. Once, we discussed how to protect the city's environment. An experienced colleague gave me some suggestions, saying I should learn more and observe more. I wrote his suggestions down in my notebook. Every day after work, I would think about what I had learned that day.

After three months, I made an important decision: I would continue working at this company. Because the environment here made me very comfortable, and I had the opportunity to learn many things. This experience was very valuable to me. Now, I can also give suggestions to new colleagues. I think helping others is a very happy thing.

title: 一个新的工作机会
body:
小王在一家小公司工作了三年，他有很多工作经验，但是公司的环境不太好，同事们很少说话。有一天，他的朋友小李给他打电话，说有一家大公司正在找人，问他有没有兴趣。

小王和小李见面后，开始讨论这个新的工作机会。小李建议小王认真考虑，因为大公司有更好的环境和更多的学习机会。小王听了以后，决定先去面试，看看自己能不能适应新的环境。

面试结束后，小王得到了这份工作。他很高兴自己做了这个决定，因为他相信新的环境会让他学到更多东西。现在他每天都很开心，也经常和同事讨论工作中的问题。
translation: Xiao Wang had worked at a small company for three years. He had a lot of work experience, but the work environment was not good, and his colleagues rarely talked to each other. One day, his friend Xiao Li called him and said a large company was hiring, asking if he was interested.

After meeting, Xiao Wang and Xiao Li began to discuss this new job opportunity. Xiao Li suggested that Xiao Wang think carefully about it, because the large company had a better environment and more learning opportunities. After hearing this, Xiao Wang decided to go for an interview first to see if he could adapt to the new environment.

After the interview, Xiao Wang got the job. He was very happy that he had made this decision, because he believed the new environment would help him learn more. Now he is happy every day and often discusses work problems with his colleagues.

title: 跨国并购案
body:
林总监站在会议室窗前，望着楼下繁忙的街道。公司即将收购一家德国老牌制造企业，这场谈判已经持续了三个月。对方代表施密特先生固执己见，坚持保留全部管理层，这让董事会十分不满。

"我们必须重新制定战略，"林总监对团队说，"不能一味强硬。这家企业虽然亏损，但在精密制造领域潜力巨大，值得我们妥协。"他提议让出两个董事会席位，换取技术专利的完全转让。这个方案让同事们陷入沉思，大家纷纷权衡利弊。

谈判桌上，施密特听完翻译后久久不语。林总监主动起身，用流利的德语说："我们欣赏贵公司的工匠精神，愿意共同守护这份传承。"最终双方达成妥协——中方控股百分之七十，德方保留核心技术团队。签字时，两位代表相视而笑。

三个月后，整合后的企业推出新一代智能机床，订单爆满。林总监在庆功宴上感慨："商业不是零和博弈，懂得适时妥协，才能释放真正的潜力。"窗外，城市的灯火比往日更加璀璨。
translation: Director Lin stood by the conference room window, looking down at the busy street below. The company was about to acquire an old German manufacturing enterprise, and the negotiations had already lasted three months. Mr. Schmidt, the representative on the other side, was stubborn and insisted on keeping all management personnel, which greatly displeased the board of directors.

"We must reformulate our strategy," Director Lin told his team. "We cannot simply be hardline. Although this company is losing money, it has tremendous potential in precision manufacturing, and is worth our compromise." He proposed giving up two board seats in exchange for complete transfer of technical patents. This plan made his colleagues fall into deep thought, and everyone began weighing the pros and cons.

At the negotiating table, Schmidt remained silent for a long time after hearing the translation. Director Lin actively stood up and said in fluent German: "We appreciate your company's craftsmanship spirit and are willing to protect this heritage together." In the end, both sides reached a compromise—Chinese side holding seventy percent of shares, German side retaining the core technical team. When signing, the two representatives smiled at each other.

Three months later, the integrated enterprise launched a new generation of intelligent machine tools, with orders flooding in. At the celebration banquet, Director Lin reflected with emotion: "Business is not a zero-sum game; knowing when to compromise can release true potential." Outside the window, the city lights shone even more brilliantly than before.

title: 跨国并购案
body:
林远站在会议室窗前，俯瞰着这座繁华的金融中心。作为集团首席战略官，他深知这次收购案关乎公司未来十年的发展。对方是一家拥有巨大潜力的新兴科技公司，但创始人团队态度强硬，谈判已经僵持了三个月。

"林总，对方又拒绝了我们的报价。"助理递来最新的邮件。林远没有立刻回应，而是仔细权衡着各种方案。如果继续施压，可能彻底谈崩；如果轻易让步，又会让董事会质疑他的能力。经过彻夜思考，他制定了一套全新的战略——不再单纯追逐控股权，而是以技术共享为核心筹码。

第二轮谈判在苏黎世举行。会议室里气氛紧张，双方代表针锋相对。林远主动提出妥协方案：保留对方创始团队的独立运营权，同时建立联合实验室。这个提议打破了僵局，对方CEO终于松口，同意就细节进行磋商。

三个月后，签约仪式如期举行。林远在致辞中说道："真正的商业智慧，不在于战胜对手，而在于找到共赢的平衡点。"这场并购不仅为公司打开了新市场，更让他明白，最高明的战略往往是懂得何时进退、如何取舍的艺术。
translation: Lin Yuan stood by the conference room window, overlooking this bustling financial center. As the group's Chief Strategy Officer, he knew this acquisition would determine the company's development over the next decade. The target was an emerging tech company with enormous potential, but its founding team was tough, and negotiations had been deadlocked for three months.

"Chief Lin, they've rejected our offer again." His assistant handed over the latest email. Lin Yuan didn't respond immediately; instead, he carefully weighed various options. If he kept pressuring them, the deal might collapse completely; if he conceded too easily, the board would question his competence. After a night of reflection, he devised a new strategy—no longer pursuing controlling shares alone, but using technology sharing as the core bargaining chip.

The second round of negotiations took place in Zurich. The atmosphere in the conference room was tense, with representatives from both sides trading sharp words. Lin Yuan proactively offered a compromise: preserving the founding team's independent operational rights while establishing a joint laboratory. This proposal broke the deadlock, and the other CEO finally relented, agreeing to discuss the details.

Three months later, the signing ceremony was held as scheduled. In his speech, Lin Yuan said, "True business wisdom lies not in defeating opponents, but in finding win-win balance." This acquisition not only opened new markets for the company but also taught him that the most brilliant strategy is the art of knowing when to advance or retreat, and how to make trade-offs.

title: 跨国并购的抉择
body:
林远作为新能源公司的首席战略官，正面临职业生涯中最艰难的决策。欧洲一家老牌车企提出收购他们苦心经营十年的电池技术部门，开价惊人，但要求完全控制核心专利。董事会为此争论不休，有人主张立即签约套现，有人坚决反对出卖未来。林远深知，这不仅是商业谈判，更关乎企业生存的底线。

在连续三天的闭门会议中，林远反复权衡各种可能性。他算了一笔账：若接受条件，公司可获得充裕现金流渡过眼前危机，却永远失去行业话语权；若拒绝，竞争对手可能趁虚而入。深夜，他独自研究对方财报，突然发现那家欧洲企业自身也深陷转型困境，这笔交易对他们而言同样紧迫。这个发现让他意识到，双方其实都有妥协的空间。

谈判桌上，林远没有直接回应报价，而是提出全新的合作框架：成立独立合资公司，中方保留核心技术所有权，仅授权使用。欧洲代表起初强硬拒绝，声称这是不可谈判的红线。林远不慌不忙，展示了自己准备的行业分析报告，指出对方若无法及时获得稳定电池供应，其电动化战略将彻底落空。经过十六小时的拉锯，双方终于在凌晨达成妥协——中方出让少数股权，但牢牢守住专利大门。

三年后，这家合资企业在全球电动车市场占据重要地位。林远在一次演讲中回忆道，那次谈判教会他最重要的一课：真正的战略不是消灭对手，而是发现彼此隐藏的潜力。当双方愿意放下傲慢、真诚寻求共赢时，看似无解的僵局反而会打开新的局面。这份领悟，比任何合同条款都更为珍贵。
translation: As Chief Strategy Officer of a new energy company, Lin Yuan was facing the most difficult decision of his career. An established European automaker had proposed acquiring their battery technology division, which they had built over ten years, offering a staggering price but demanding complete control of core patents. The board was divided: some advocated signing immediately to cash out, while others firmly opposed selling the future. Lin Yuan knew this was not merely a business negotiation, but concerned the bottom line of the company's survival.

During three consecutive days of closed-door meetings, Lin Yuan repeatedly weighed various possibilities. He calculated the accounts: accepting the terms would bring abundant cash flow to survive the immediate crisis, but would permanently lose industry voice; rejecting it might allow competitors to take advantage. Late at night, he studied the other party's financial reports alone and suddenly discovered that the European company was also deeply troubled by its own transformation—this deal was equally urgent for them. This realization made him understand that both sides actually had room for compromise.

At the negotiation table, Lin Yuan did not directly respond to the offer, but instead proposed a new cooperation framework: establishing an independent joint venture with the Chinese side retaining core technology ownership and only licensing its use. The European representatives initially refused firmly, claiming this was a non-negotiable red line. Lin Yuan calmly presented his prepared industry analysis report, pointing out that without timely access to stable battery supply, their electrification strategy would completely fail. After sixteen hours of back-and-forth, both sides finally reached a compromise in the early morning hours—the Chinese side transferred minority equity but firmly guarded the patent door.

Three years later, this joint venture held an important position in the global electric vehicle market. Recalling the experience in a speech, Lin Yuan said the most important lesson that negotiation taught him was: true strategy is not about eliminating opponents, but about discovering each other's hidden potential. When both parties are willing to put aside arrogance and sincerely seek mutual benefit, seemingly unsolvable deadlocks will instead open up new possibilities. This insight was more precious than any contract clause.

title: 第一次去银行
body:
李伟今天第一次去银行取钱。他要给好朋友买生日礼物，所以带了很重的包裹。银行里人很多，他找了个角落坐下，取出笔记本计算金额。他想起家里的绿萝已经长得很长了，必须记得浇水。虽然事情多，但他决定耐心等候。

等了半个小时，终于轮到李伟。服务员的态度有些差，说话也不清楚。李伟只好递过身份证、银行卡和填好的表格。他看着工作人员操作电脑，心里有些着急。为了节省时间，他轻声请求对方快点办完。对方点点头，继续处理。

很快，业务办好了。李伟接过现金和凭条，把借用的笔还给了柜台人员。他走出银行大门，阳光照在脸上。虽然过程不顺利，但拿到钱后他感到很轻松。他决定立刻去商场挑选礼物，希望朋友喜欢这份心意
translation: Li Wei went to the bank for the first time today to withdraw money. He needed to buy a birthday gift for a good friend, so he brought a heavy package. There were many people at the bank, so he found a corner to sit down and took out a notebook to calculate the amount. He remembered that the pothos at home had grown very long and he must remember to water it. Although he had many things to do, he decided to wait patiently.

After waiting for half an hour, it was finally his turn. The clerk's attitude was somewhat poor and her speech was not clear. Li Wei could only hand over his ID card, bank card, and the filled form. He watched the staff operate the computer and felt a bit anxious because time was running out. To save time, he politely asked them to finish quickly. The staff nodded and continued processing.

Soon, the transaction was done. Li Wei took the cash and receipt, and returned the borrowed pen to the counter staff. He walked out of the bank, and the sunlight warmed his face. Although the process was not smooth, he felt very relaxed after getting the money. He decided to go to the mall immediately to pick a gift, hoping his friend would like it and have a happy birthday.

title: 小明买吉他
body:
小明想买一把吉他，今天他决定去银行取钱。出门的时候，他背上很重的背包，里面装着课本和笔记本。天气虽然有点冷，但他心里很高兴，因为很快就能实现自己的愿望。走到街上，他忍不住想：如果今天能买到喜欢的吉他，周末就可以给朋友们表演了。

去音乐商店的路非常长，他走了大约四十分钟。路上人来人往，小明只好慢慢走。虽然时间有点紧张，但他还有两小时才关门，所以一点也不着急。商店里的吉他款式很多，质量也不差，他挑了一把深棕色的，琴身光滑又好看。

付完钱以后，小明抱着吉他开心地往回走。他对朋友说：“学音乐并不简单，但只要每天坚持练习，一定会进步的。”回到家，他立刻坐在椅子上弹了一首简单的曲子。窗外的风吹进来，他觉得很满足，明天还要继续练习。
translation: Xiao Ming wanted to buy a guitar, so today he decided to go to the bank to withdraw some money. When he left, he put a heavy backpack on his shoulders, inside which were his textbooks and notebooks. Although the weather was a bit cold, he felt very happy in his heart because he would soon be able to realize his wish. Walking on the street, he couldn't help thinking: if he could buy his favorite guitar today, he could perform for his friends this weekend.

The road to the music store was very long, and he walked for about forty minutes. There were many people on the way, so Xiao Ming had to walk slowly. Although time was a little tight, he still had two hours before the store closed, so he was not in a hurry at all. There were many styles of guitars in the store, and the quality was not bad either. He picked a dark brown one with a smooth and beautiful body.

After paying, Xiao Ming walked back happily, holding his guitar. He told his friends, "Learning music is not simple, but as long as you practice every day, you will definitely improve." When he got home, he immediately sat on a chair and played a simple tune. The wind blew in through the window, and he felt very satisfied. He still needed to continue practicing tomorrow.

title: 李明的银行工作
body:
李明今年二十五岁，在一家大银行工作。他每天都很忙，但工资不高。有一天，经理对他说："你的工作能力还差一点儿，需要继续努力。"李明听了很难过，但他没有放弃。

几个月后，李明的机会来了。一位重要的客户来银行办理业务，因为资料太重，老人搬不动。李明主动帮忙，还耐心地解释每一个步骤。客户非常满意，写了很多表扬的话。经理看到以后，决定让李明负责更重要的工作。

现在李明已经长了很多经验，不再是个新手了。虽然工作还是很忙，但他觉得每一天都有意义。他常常对自己说："只要用心，就没有做不到的事。"他的故事告诉我们，开始的时候可能不够好，但只要坚持，一定会有好的结果。
translation: Li Ming is twenty-five years old and works at a large bank. He is busy every day, but his salary is not high. One day, his manager told him: "Your work ability is still a little lacking; you need to keep working hard." Li Ming felt sad hearing this, but he did not give up.

A few months later, Li Ming's opportunity came. An important elderly customer came to the bank to handle business, but the documents were too heavy for the old man to carry. Li Ming took the initiative to help, and patiently explained every step. The customer was very satisfied and wrote a lot of praise. After seeing this, the manager decided to let Li Ming take charge of more important work.

Now Li Ming has grown a lot of experience and is no longer a newcomer. Although work is still busy, he feels that every day has meaning. He often says to himself: "As long as you put your heart into it, there is nothing you cannot do." His story tells us that you may not be good enough at the beginning, but as long as you persist, there will surely be good results.

title: 小猫来了
body: 我家有一只小猫。它叫小白，是白色的。早上，小白饿了，它对我叫：“喵！”我给它牛奶喝。小白很高兴，它喝了牛奶，然后睡觉了。下午，我的朋友来了。她看见小白，说：“你的猫真可爱！”我们一起和小猫玩。晚上，小白又饿了，我又给它牛奶。小白是我的好朋友。
translation: I have a little cat at home. It's called Little White and is white. In the morning, Little White was hungry and meowed at me: "Meow!" I gave it milk to drink. Little White was very happy, it drank the milk and then went to sleep. In the afternoon, my friend came. She saw Little White and said: "Your cat is really cute!" We played with the little cat together. In the evening, Little White was hungry again, and I gave it milk again. Little White is my good friend.

body: 王小姐住在北京，她有一只小猫。这只猫很小，是白色的。一天早上，猫跑出去了。王小姐很着急，她去找猫。她在公园里看见一只白色的猫，那是她的猫！她高兴地说："你在这儿！"她把猫抱回家，给它水喝。猫很高兴，它喜欢这个家。

title: 雨中的邂逅
body:
上个周末，我一个人去山里散步，没想到天空突然下起了大雨。我赶紧跑到附近的一座亭子躲雨，浑身都被淋湿了。正当我拧着衣服上的水时，一位陌生的朋友走了进来。我们互相点了点头，谁也没有说话。

过了一会儿，雨还是没有停。我忍不住开口问他是不是也在等朋友，他说其实是来山里散心的。我们聊了起来，原来他是一家公司的经理，最近工作压力很大。这次邂逅让我觉得很意外，因为平时我很少和陌生人聊天。他问我愿不愿意一起去山下的茶馆坐坐，我踌躇了一下，但看着外面的雨，还是答应了。

在茶馆里，我们喝着热茶，聊了很多关于生活和梦想的话题。他说这次偶遇让他心情好多了，还邀请我以后去他公司参观。雨停后，我们交换了联系方式，约定下次再见面。这次意外的相遇，让我相信生活中总会有美好的惊喜。
translation: Last weekend, I went hiking alone in the mountains when it suddenly started raining heavily. I quickly ran to a nearby pavilion to take shelter, completely soaked. Just as I was wringing water out of my clothes, a stranger walked in. We nodded at each other, but neither of us spoke.

After a while, the rain still hadn't stopped. I couldn't help asking if he was also waiting for a friend. He said he had actually come to the mountains to clear his mind. We started chatting, and I learned he was a company manager under a lot of work pressure lately. This chance encounter surprised me, as I rarely talk to strangers. He asked if I'd like to go to a teahouse at the foot of the mountain together. I hesitated for a moment, but looking at the rain outside, I agreed.

In the teahouse, we drank hot tea and talked a lot about life and dreams. He said this unexpected meeting had lifted his spirits and invited me to visit his company someday. After the rain stopped, we exchanged contact information and made plans to meet again. This unexpected encounter made me believe that life always holds beautiful surprises.

title: 雨中的邂逅
body:
那是一个秋天的傍晚，天空飘着细雨。你独自走在回家的路上，手里没有伞，衣服渐渐被雨水打湿。就在你准备加快脚步的时候，突然看见一个熟悉的身影站在咖啡馆门口——那是你多年未见的老朋友小林。你们曾在大学时代形影不离，毕业后却失去了联系。这次意外的邂逅让你们都愣了一下，然后同时露出了惊喜的笑容。

你踌躇着要不要先开口，毕竟已经五年没见了。小林却毫不犹豫地朝你走来，热情地拍了拍你的肩膀，邀请你进咖啡馆坐坐。你们点了两杯热咖啡，开始聊起各自的生活。原来小林就住在这附近，而你也刚搬到这个城市工作。你们感叹命运的奇妙，竟然在这么大的城市里偶然相遇。

雨越下越大，但你们聊得越来越投机。临走时，你们交换了新的联系方式，约定周末一起去爬山。你走出咖啡馆，发现雨已经小了。虽然衣服还是湿的，但心里却感到无比温暖。有时候，生活中的美好就藏在这样的邂逅里，只需要一点勇气，就能找回珍贵的友谊。
translation: It was an autumn evening, with light rain falling from the sky. You were walking home alone, without an umbrella, and your clothes were gradually getting wet from the rain. Just as you were about to quicken your pace, you suddenly saw a familiar figure standing at the entrance of a café—it was your old friend Xiaolin, whom you hadn't seen for many years. You two had been inseparable during college, but lost touch after graduation. This unexpected encounter made you both freeze for a moment, then simultaneously break into surprised smiles.

You hesitated about whether to speak first, after all, it had been five years since you last met. But Xiaolin walked toward you without hesitation, warmly patted you on the shoulder, and invited you inside the café to sit down. You ordered two cups of hot coffee and began chatting about your respective lives. It turned out Xiaolin lived nearby, and you had just moved to this city for work. You both marveled at the wonder of fate, having accidentally met in such a big city.

The rain grew heavier and heavier, but your conversation became more and more enjoyable. When leaving, you exchanged new contact information and made plans to go hiking together on the weekend. You walked out of the café and found that the rain had already lightened. Although your clothes were still wet, your heart felt incredibly warm. Sometimes, the beauty in life hides in such chance encounters—it only takes a little courage to recover precious friendship.

title: 延误的航班
body:
去年夏天，我们全家决定去云南旅行。妈妈提前两个月就开始计划这次旅行，她预订了机票、酒店，还联系了一位当地的导游。爸爸说这次旅行的预算是一万元，包括所有的交通、住宿和吃饭的费用。我们都非常期待这次旅行，因为云南的风景特别有名。

出发那天早上，我们早早地起床，检查了好几次行李。爸爸把护照、身份证和钱包都放在了随身携带的背包里。妈妈则反复确认酒店预订的信息，生怕出什么差错。我们叫了一辆出租车，高高兴兴地去了机场。

到了机场，我们发现大厅里挤满了人。广播里不断传来航班延误的消息，原来是因为天气不好，很多飞机都不能按时起飞。我们赶紧跑到服务台询问，工作人员告诉我们，我们的航班也会延误，具体时间还不确定。

听到这个消息，妹妹差点哭了出来。她本来特别期待这次旅行，还在网上查了很多云南的风景照片。爸爸安慰她说："没关系，延误是常有的事，我们可以先在机场逛逛，看看有没有好看的纪念品。"

我们只好在机场等待。妈妈去买了几杯咖啡，我们坐在椅子上聊天。我注意到机场里有一家卖当地特产的小店，就拉着妹妹过去看。那里有很多有趣的小东西，妹妹选了一个漂亮的钥匙扣作为纪念品。

大约等了四个小时，广播终于通知我们可以登机了。大家都松了一口气，赶紧拿起行李往登机口跑。虽然延误了很久，但是飞机上的导游告诉我们，云南的天气已经变好了，不会影响我们的行程。

到达云南的时候，已经是晚上了。我们本来计划下午去古城逛逛，但是因为航班延误，这个计划只能取消了。导游建议我们明天早点出发，把今天没去的地方补上。我们都同意了，毕竟安全最重要。

第二天一早，我们就开始了正式的旅行。云南的风景真的太美了，有蓝天白云，还有绿色的山和清澈的水。导游带我们去了一个很有名的湖，我们在那里拍了很多照片。虽然第一天的行程受到了影响，但是后面的几天都非常顺利。

这次旅行让我明白了一个道理：旅行中总会遇到一些意外，比如天气不好、航班延误等等。但是只要大家在一起，保持好心情，这些困难都能克服。我们买了很多纪念品带回家，每次看到这些纪念品，我都会想起这次难忘的家庭旅行。
translation: Last summer, our whole family decided to travel to Yunnan. Mom started planning this trip two months in advance. She booked the plane tickets and hotel, and also contacted a local tour guide. Dad said the budget for this trip was ten thousand yuan, including all transportation, accommodation, and meals. We were all very much looking forward to this trip because Yunnan's scenery is especially famous.

On the morning of our departure, we got up early and checked our luggage several times. Dad put the passports, ID cards, and wallet in his carry-on backpack. Mom repeatedly confirmed the hotel reservation information, afraid something might go wrong. We called a taxi and happily went to the airport.

When we arrived at the airport, we found the hall packed with people. The broadcast kept announcing flight delays; it turned out that because of bad weather, many planes couldn't take off on time. We hurried to the service desk to ask, and the staff told us that our flight would also be delayed, with the exact time still uncertain.

Hearing this news, my little sister almost cried. She had been especially looking forward to this trip and had looked up many photos of Yunnan's scenery online. Dad comforted her, saying, "It's okay, delays are common. We can walk around the airport first and see if there are any nice souvenirs."

We had no choice but to wait at the airport. Mom went to buy a few cups of coffee, and we sat on chairs chatting. I noticed a small shop selling local specialties in the airport and pulled my sister over to look. There were many interesting little things there, and my sister chose a pretty keychain as a souvenir.

After waiting about four hours, the broadcast finally announced that we could board. Everyone breathed a sigh of relief, quickly picked up their luggage, and ran to the boarding gate. Although the delay was long, the tour guide on the plane told us that the weather in Yunnan had already improved and wouldn't affect our itinerary.

When we arrived in Yunnan, it was already evening. We had originally planned to visit the ancient town in the afternoon, but because of the flight delay, this plan had to be canceled. The tour guide suggested we set out early tomorrow to make up for the places we missed today. We all agreed; after all, safety is the most important.

Early the next morning, we began our formal trip. Yunnan's scenery was truly beautiful, with blue sky and white clouds, green mountains, and clear water. The tour guide took us to a very famous lake, where we took many photos. Although the first day's schedule was affected, the following few days went very smoothly.

This trip taught me a truth: there will always be some unexpected events during travel, such as bad weather, flight delays, and so on. But as long as everyone is together and keeps a good mood, these difficulties can be overcome. We bought many souvenirs to bring home, and every time I see these souvenirs, I think of this unforgettable family trip.

title: 延误的航班
body:
去年夏天，我们一家人决定去云南旅行。爸爸提前两个月就开始计划这次假期，他仔细研究了天气情况，还预订了性价比很高的酒店。妈妈负责整理行李，她把每个人的衣服都叠得整整齐齐，还提醒我一定要带好护照。

出发那天，我们早早来到机场。大厅里人来人往，到处都是拖着行李箱的旅客。爸爸去办理登机手续，妈妈则坐在椅子上休息。我兴奋地看着窗外的飞机，心想马上就能看到美丽的风景了。

可是等了很久，广播里突然传来消息：由于暴雨天气，我们的航班延误了。爸爸皱起眉头，担心地说这会影响后面的行程。原来他已经请好了导游，还安排好了每天的参观路线。

妈妈安慰我们说："没关系，安全第一。"她打开背包，拿出准备好的零食分给大家。我们一边吃一边聊天，时间倒也不算难熬。我还趁机在机场商店逛了逛，看有没有合适的纪念品可以买。

三小时后，飞机终于起飞了。到达昆明时，天已经黑了。导游在机场出口等我们，她笑着说："你们来得正好，明天早上我带你们去看最美的风景。"我们虽然疲惫，但听到这话都很开心。

第二天一早，阳光明媚，天气特别好。导游带我们去了石林，那里的石头形状奇特，像各种各样的动物。我拍了很多照片，爸爸则认真地听导游讲解每个景点的历史故事。

中午吃饭时，爸爸算了一下这次旅行的花费。虽然航班延误让我们多付了一晚酒店钱，但总体还在预算之内。妈妈笑着说："只要大家平安，多花一点也没关系。"

接下来的几天，我们游览了大理古城和丽江古城。我在古城里买了几个很有特色的纪念品，一个是手工制作的银手镯，另一个是画着当地风景的扇子。妈妈说我越来越会挑选东西了。

旅行结束时，我们都有些舍不得离开。虽然开头遇到了航班延误的小麻烦，但这次家庭旅行依然让我们留下了美好的回忆。爸爸说他已经开始计划明年的旅行了，希望下次一切顺利。
translation: Last summer, our family decided to travel to Yunnan. Dad started planning this vacation two months in advance. He carefully studied the weather conditions and also booked hotels with great value for money. Mom was in charge of packing luggage. She folded everyone's clothes neatly and reminded me to make sure to bring my passport.

On the day of departure, we arrived at the airport early. The hall was crowded with travelers dragging their suitcases everywhere. Dad went to check us in while Mom sat in a chair to rest. I excitedly watched the planes outside the window, thinking that I would soon see beautiful scenery.

But after waiting for a long time, an announcement suddenly came over the loudspeaker: due to heavy rain weather, our flight was delayed. Dad frowned and worried that this would affect our later itinerary. It turned out he had already hired a tour guide and arranged sightseeing routes for each day.

Mom comforted us, saying: "It's okay, safety comes first." She opened her backpack and took out the snacks she had prepared to share with everyone. We chatted while eating, so the time wasn't too hard to bear. I also took the opportunity to browse the airport shops to see if there were any suitable souvenirs to buy.

Three hours later, the plane finally took off. When we arrived in Kunming, it was already dark. The tour guide was waiting for us at the airport exit. She smiled and said: "You came at just the right time. Tomorrow morning I'll take you to see the most beautiful scenery." Although we were tired, we were all very happy to hear this.

The next morning, the sun was shining and the weather was especially nice. The tour guide took us to the Stone Forest, where the rocks had strange shapes like various animals. I took many photos, while Dad listened carefully to the tour guide's explanations of the history behind each attraction.

At lunch, Dad calculated the expenses for this trip. Although the flight delay cost us an extra night at the hotel, the total was still within budget. Mom smiled and said: "As long as everyone is safe, spending a little more doesn't matter."

Over the following days, we visited Dali Ancient City and Lijiang Ancient City. I bought several very distinctive souvenirs in the ancient city—one was a handmade silver bracelet, and another was a fan painted with local scenery. Mom said I was getting better at picking things out.

When the trip ended, we were all a bit reluctant to leave. Although we encountered the small trouble of a flight delay at the beginning, this family trip still left us with beautiful memories. Dad said he had already started planning next year's trip and hoped everything would go smoothly next time.

title: 延误的航班
body:
去年夏天，我们全家计划了一次去云南的旅行。爸爸提前两个月就开始准备，他认真地研究了天气情况，还预订了性价比很高的酒店。妈妈说这次旅行预算有限，所以我们要节省一点，但爸爸坚持说美丽的风景值得多花一些钱。

出发那天早上，我们四点就起床了。我负责检查护照和身份证，弟弟帮忙收拾行李。虽然行李很多，但每个人都带着期待的心情。我们打车去机场，一路上爸爸不停地看手表，生怕迟到。

到了机场，我们发现大厅里挤满了人。广播里传来消息，由于天气原因，我们预订的航班延误了。工作人员说可能要等六个小时，具体时间还不确定。妈妈叹了口气，弟弟差点哭出来。

爸爸很快冷静下来，他带着我们去机场的餐厅吃早餐。他说既然已经来了，就不要让延误影响心情。我们一边吃米线，一边讨论到了云南要买的纪念品。我想买一件民族风的衣服，爸爸想要茶叶，妈妈则对银饰很感兴趣。

吃完饭后，爸爸联系了当地的导游，告诉他我们会晚到。那位导游很理解，说他会调整明天的行程。我们决定在机场逛逛商店，看看有没有合适的礼物带给亲戚。虽然延误很讨厌，但一家人在一起聊天也挺开心的。

下午两点，航班终于可以登机了。飞机起飞后，我从窗户看到了美丽的云海，心情一下子好了起来。空姐发饮料的时候，爸爸还开玩笑说这次延误让我们多看了几个小时机场的风景，也算是特别的体验。

到达云南的时候，天已经黑了。导游举着牌子在出口等我们，他热情地帮我们拿行李，还给我们每人送了一小包鲜花饼作为欢迎礼物。他说虽然今天耽误了时间，但明天的行程会更轻松，因为晚上的古城灯火通明，别有一番风味。

那天的延误让我们比计划晚到了八个小时，但也让我们学会了随机应变。后来每次家庭聚会，我们都会提起这次特别的经历。妈妈说她终于明白，旅行中最重要的不是严格的计划，而是一家人在一起的时光。

现在我的书桌上还放着那次旅行买的纪念品——一个小小的风铃。每当风吹过来，它发出清脆的声音，我就会想起那个延误的航班，想起机场里爸爸说的那句话：好的风景，有时候需要多等一会儿才能看到。
translation: Last summer, our whole family planned a trip to Yunnan. Dad started preparing two months in advance. He carefully studied the weather conditions and also booked a hotel with great value for money. Mom said this trip had a limited budget, so we needed to save a bit, but Dad insisted that beautiful scenery was worth spending more on.

On the morning of departure, we woke up at four o'clock. I was responsible for checking the passports and ID cards, while my younger brother helped pack the luggage. Although there was a lot of luggage, everyone was in a mood of anticipation. We took a taxi to the airport. Along the way, Dad kept checking his watch, afraid of being late.

When we arrived at the airport, we found the hall packed with people. An announcement came over the loudspeaker: due to weather conditions, our booked flight was delayed. The staff said we might have to wait six hours, and the exact time was still uncertain. Mom sighed, and my brother almost started crying.

Dad quickly calmed down and took us to the airport restaurant for breakfast. He said since we were already here, we shouldn't let the delay affect our mood. While eating rice noodles, we discussed what souvenirs to buy in Yunnan. I wanted to buy an ethnic-style dress, Dad wanted tea, and Mom was very interested in silver jewelry.

After breakfast, Dad contacted the local tour guide and told him we would arrive late. The guide was very understanding and said he would adjust tomorrow's itinerary. We decided to walk around the airport shops and see if there were suitable gifts for relatives. Although the delay was annoying, it was quite nice for the family to chat together.

At two in the afternoon, the flight was finally ready for boarding. After the plane took off, I saw beautiful sea of clouds from the window, and my mood immediately improved. When the flight attendant served drinks, Dad even joked that this delay let us see the airport scenery for a few extra hours, which was a special experience.

When we arrived in Yunnan, it was already dark. The tour guide was holding a sign waiting for us at the exit. He enthusiastically helped us with our luggage and gave each of us a small package of flower cakes as a welcome gift. He said although today was delayed, tomorrow's itinerary would be more relaxed, because the ancient city at night was brightly lit and had a special charm.

That day's delay made us arrive eight hours later than planned, but it also taught us to adapt to circumstances. Later at every family gathering, we would bring up this special experience. Mom said she finally understood that the most important thing in travel is not a strict plan, but the time spent together as a family.

Now there's still a souvenir from that trip on my desk—a small wind chime. Whenever the wind blows and it makes a crisp sound, I think of that delayed flight and what Dad said at the airport: good scenery sometimes needs a little more waiting to be seen.

title: 在德国学社会学的日子
body:
李明是一位从中国的移民，他特意选择到德国学习社会学。他发现德国社会非常重视个人主义，每个人的地位都受到法律保护。为了提高自己的阅读能力，他每天都去图书馆，而口语能力则通过和身边的朋友练习。

有一次，他的教授讲了一个关于监狱改革的理论，说实践比空谈更重要。李明觉得这个理由很有道理，但他也注意到德国社会存在一些问题，比如环境污染让一些城市变得难看。更奇怪的是，网上有人用表情包来讨论严肃话题，他觉得这种做法太不正式，甚至想直接怼回去。

不过，李明很快学会了理解当地文化。他发现德国人虽然看起来洋气，但反对暴力，遇到不公平的事会反抗，而不是沉默。有一次讨论移民政策时，大家干脆坦诚地交换意见，没有人觉得尴尬。

这段经历给李明带来了很多改变。他不再认为西方理论都是完美的，也学会了尊重不同观点。最终，他的研究论文获得了好评，因为他把书本知识和社会现实结合得很好。
translation: Li Ming is an immigrant from China who specially chose to study sociology in Germany. He discovered that German society places great importance on individualism, and everyone's status is protected by law. To improve his reading ability, he went to the library every day, while he practiced his speaking ability with friends around him.

Once, his professor talked about a theory regarding prison reform, saying that practice is more important than empty talk. Li Ming found this reason quite convincing, but he also noticed some problems in German society, such as environmental pollution making some cities look ugly. Even stranger, some people online used meme images to discuss serious topics, which he found too informal and even wanted to talk back to directly.

However, Li Ming soon learned to understand the local culture. He discovered that although Germans may look stylish, they oppose violence and will resist when encountering unfairness rather than staying silent. Once when discussing immigration policy, everyone simply exchanged opinions honestly without anyone feeling awkward.

This experience brought Li Ming many changes. He no longer believed that Western theories were perfect, and also learned to respect different viewpoints. In the end, his research paper received good reviews because he combined book knowledge with social reality very well.

title: 德国的社会
body:
李明是一位从山东移民到德国的年轻人。他特意选择在柏林大学学习社会学，想深入了解德国的社会结构。他发现，德国社会非常重视个人主义，每个人的地位和权利都受到法律保护。

有一次，他在课堂上讨论环境保护问题。教授提到，德国在减少污染方面有很多实践经验。李明却站起来怼教授，说这些理论听起来很洋气，但身边很多工厂依然存在难看的废水排放。他的口语能力还不够好，说得有些结巴，但阅读能力让他能引用大量数据。

教授没有生气，反而欣赏他的反抗精神。教授解释说，德国曾经历过暴力冲突的历史，所以社会学会了用对话代替对抗。如果有人因为犯罪进了监狱，出狱后仍有机会重新获得社会地位，这就是德国社会的包容性。

李明明白了，干脆把这次讨论做成表情包发到网上，没想到火了。他意识到，移民带来的不仅是人口流动，更是不同文化的碰撞。这种交流让他成长，也让德国社会更加多元。
translation: Li Ming is a young man who immigrated to Germany from Shandong. He specially chose to study sociology at Berlin University, wanting to deeply understand Germany's social structure. He discovered that German society places great importance on individualism, and everyone's status and rights are protected by law.

Once, he discussed environmental protection issues in class. The professor mentioned that Germany has a lot of practical experience in reducing pollution. But Li Ming stood up to talk back to the professor, saying these theories sounded very stylish, but many factories around him still had unsightly wastewater discharge. His speaking ability was not good enough, and he spoke somewhat haltingly, but his reading ability allowed him to cite large amounts of data.

The professor was not angry; instead, he appreciated his spirit of resistance. The professor explained that Germany had experienced a history of violent conflict, so society learned to use dialogue instead of confrontation. If someone went to prison for a crime, they still had the opportunity to regain their social status after release—this is the inclusiveness of German society.

Li Ming understood and simply turned this discussion into a meme and posted it online, unexpectedly becoming popular. He realized that immigration brings not only population movement but also the collision of different cultures. This exchange helped him grow and also made German society more diverse.

title: 德国室友的社会课
body:
去年，我移民到德国，特意选了一所注重实践的大学。我的室友汉斯是个理论家，总把个人主义挂在嘴边，却从不关心身边的环境污染问题。每当我用表情包怼他的双标时，他就说我有暴力倾向，这理由实在难看。

我们的冲突在讨论监狱改革时爆发了。汉斯认为暴力犯罪者不该有学习机会，我干脆反抗他的观点，指出教育能带来真正的改变。我提到德国社会给移民的地位太低，阅读能力比口语能力更重要，他却觉得我崇洋媚外。

周末，汉斯带我去他老家。那座洋气的小城曾是反抗纳粹的据点，老人特意给我们讲历史。我终于明白，德国的社会进步不是靠理论，而是靠普通人把平等理念付诸实践。

现在我们成了朋友。他不再用表情包调侃我的德语，我也学会了用德国人的方式讨论问题。这段经历让我明白，真正的理解需要双方放下偏见，在对话中寻找共识。
translation: Last year, I immigrated to Germany and specially chose a university that emphasizes practical learning. My roommate Hans was a theorist who always talked about individualism but never cared about the environmental pollution around him. Whenever I called him out with memes for his double standards, he would say I had violent tendencies—this reason was truly unsightly.

Our conflict erupted when discussing prison reform. Hans believed that violent criminals shouldn't have educational opportunities, so I simply resisted his view, pointing out that education could bring about real change. I mentioned that immigrants' status in German society was too low and that reading ability mattered more than speaking ability, but he thought I was being overly Western-worshipping.

On the weekend, Hans took me to his hometown. That stylish small town had been a stronghold of resistance against the Nazis, and an elderly person specially told us about its history. I finally understood that Germany's social progress didn't rely on theory, but on ordinary people putting the concept of equality into practice.

Now we are friends. He no longer teases my German with memes, and I've learned to discuss issues the German way. This experience made me realize that true understanding requires both sides to put aside prejudice and seek consensus through dialogue.
